spec_match.rationale: The shorthand-collapse logic (corner → corner-top/bottom → per-corner) matches CSS Borders 4, but the shape list offers an invented 'straight' keyword and omits the spec's real 'square' and superellipse() values — verified on Chromium 141, where CSS.supports('corner-shape','square') and 'superellipse(2)' are true and 'straight' is false.

interactive.rationale: Per-corner selects and radius sliders, three presets, a live preview driven through the corner-*-shape longhands, a generated shortest rule, and a computed-longhand read-back table all update on interaction.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index promises collapse/expand behaviour with generated CSS and computed read-back, and the page delivers exactly that.

edge_cases.rationale: Three support tiers are handled (shorthand / longhand-only / neither), but selecting the bogus 'straight' value silently leaves the previous shape applied while the generated rule claims straight — a mismatch between the copyable CSS and the rendered preview.

references.rationale: Links https://chromestatus.com/feature/5152215540039680 and the CSS Borders 4 corner-shaping section.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite is strong: parse checks for every shorthand tier plus computed-style proofs that the shorthand sets both longhands, scopes to one corner, and that logical radii remap with writing mode.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp) via CDP: banner correctly reports 'corner-shape works but the shorthands do not'; Ticket stub collapsed to 'corner: scoop 26px', switching top-left to notch expanded to corner-top-left/right + corner-bottom, and the computed table read back notch/scoop per corner from the live element; console clean, no exceptions; screenshots at both viewports.

telemetry_health.rationale: Renders log declaration counts and emit showcaseTelemetry.assert('corners-rendered', …) with shorthand/shape support flags.

design_system.rationale: Token colours throughout; the secondary button class overrides background and color together; selects and sliders meet the 44px minimum.

accessibility.rationale: Every select and slider is inside a labelled control with a visible value readout, the computed table has caption and scopes, and the summary is an aria-live output.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: 0px horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3 and 1280x800 over CDP; the corner grid stacks to one column on mobile with unclipped controls in both screenshots.

openQuestions.title: Replace the invented 'straight' corner-shape value with the spec's 'square' (and expose superellipse())
openQuestions.detail: The SHAPES list is ['round','bevel','scoop','notch','squircle','straight'], but CSS Borders 4 defines round | scoop | bevel | notch | square | squircle | superellipse(). Empirically on Chromium 141 (which ships corner-shape): CSS.supports('corner-shape','square')===true, 'superellipse(2)'===true, 'straight'===false. Choosing 'straight' therefore generates a rule that no browser parses while the preview silently keeps the previously applied shape — the generated 'what you would paste' CSS is wrong. Swap 'straight' for 'square' and consider a superellipse(k) slider as the advanced angle. This is the stale-enum-vocabulary defect class from the anti-regression list.

openQuestions.title: Make the Ticket stub preset actually per-corner
openQuestions.detail: The button's own comment says 'scooped ends, square top and bottom. The classic case for per-corner control', but the preset sets all four corners to scoop 26px, so the rule collapses to a single 'corner: scoop 26px' — verified over CDP. Set only the two left (or bottom) corners to scoop and leave the others square/round so the preset demonstrates the per-corner and per-edge shorthands it was written to motivate.

summary: Genuinely interactive builder with honest three-tier capability handling, verified on Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp) at http://localhost:3000/v155/css-corner-shorthand-properties/corner-builder/: shorthands unsupported (7/8 suite assertions fail honestly on the /conformance/ route), corner-shape longhands supported and driving the preview, computed read-back real, console clean, both device classes overflow-free. Two content defects: an invented 'straight' shape value where the spec says 'square' (major — the copyable CSS is invalid and the preview silently disagrees), and a Ticket-stub preset that contradicts its own per-corner premise by setting all four corners identically.
